title: Does Stealth Ability Drive Sabotage Inconsistency? Testing the Stealth Bottleneck Hypothesis

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Elegantly isolates a single variable (stealth requirement) to test whether monitoring is a high-leverage intervention. If stealth is the bottleneck, monitoring is justified; if not, safety margins are thinner. Extremely clear and actionable theory of change.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires building an AI R&D sabotage evaluation environment with two conditions. The environment itself is expert-level engineering. Running enough trials for statistical significance adds compute and time costs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The experimental design is clean (two conditions, same tasks). If the evaluation environment were pre-built, this would be very narrow. But building the environment from scratch is the bottleneck. Could be feasible if using an existing framework like ControlArena.
